subject: Math
skill: Inference From Sample Statistics And Margin Of Error
prompt: A study was conducted on the heights of different types of trees in a forest. A random sample of trees were selected and tagged so that none were measured more than once. The sample contained $220$ oak trees, of which $45%$ were taller than $15$ meters. Which of the following conclusions is best supported by the sample data?

choices.A: The average height of all trees in the forest is approximately $15$ meters.
choices.B: Approximately $45%$ of all trees in the forest are taller than $15$ meters.
choices.C: Approximately $45%$ of all oak trees in the forest are taller than $15$ meters.
choices.D: The majority of all trees in the forest are shorter than $15$ meters.

explanation: Choice C is correct. The sample of $220$ oak trees was selected at random from all the oak trees in the forest, and since $45\%$ of the oak trees in the sample were taller than $15$ meters, it can be concluded that approximately $45\%$ of all oak trees in the forest are taller than $15$ meters.
